top.help:
OCI Generative AI is a fully managed service that provides a set of state-of-the-art, customizable large language models (LLMs) that cover a wide range of use cases for text generation, summarization, and text embeddings.

Use the Generative AI service management CLI to create and manage [dedicated AI clusters], [endpoints], [custom models], and [work requests] in the Generative AI service. For example, create a custom model by fine-tuning an out-of-the-box model using your own data, on a fine-tuning dedicated AI cluster. Then, create a hosting dedicated AI cluster with an endpoint to host your custom model.

To access your custom model endpoints, or to try the out-of-the-box models to generate text, summarize, and create text embeddings see the [Generative AI Inference CLI].

To learn more about the service, see the [Generative AI documentation].

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation creates, modifies or deletes a resource that has a defined lifecycle state. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the resource reaches a given lifecycle state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state CREATING --wait-for-state FAILED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the resource to reach the lifecycle state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the resource has reached the lifecycle state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

params.name: active_artifact_time_created
params.help:
The date and time the artifact was created.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

sandbox-warm-pool create.help:
Creates a named MANAGED or CUSTOM pool. MANAGED uses the service-provided python-3.11 runtime and requires containerImage to be omitted. CUSTOM requires a digest-pinned containerImage. Project-wide shape capacity limits include named pools of both types and reserved default pools. Type, image, shape and name are immutable. The CP atomically persists CREATING and a Work Request, then its workflow prepares an immutable pool-owned template and applies the pool configuration. Each MANAGED pool has a distinct template based on the service runtime configuration, isolated from other pools of the same shape. ACTIVE means configuration was applied and verified; it does not require ready members, a successful image boot or available cluster capacity. Zero capacity pauses idle prewarming. An ACTIVE named pool can still create Sandboxes through cold fallback when its applied template is available. Retry identity and configuration are persisted atomically. Within the 24-hour retry-token validity period, the same token and input identify the original pool id, including after name reuse. A retry never creates or selects a replacement pool. A retry after the original pool is deleted returns 409; changed input with the same token conflicts. Reserved default names cannot be reused for either type. 
[Command Reference](createSandboxWarmPool)

params.name: type
params.help: MANAGED uses the service-provided python-3.11 runtime. CUSTOM uses a customer-provided containerImage. Both types support named pool creation. [required]

params.name: shape
params.help: Compute shape for each idle Sandbox member. [required]

params.name: desired_capacity
params.help: Desired number of idle members. Zero pauses idle prewarming. Once the pool is ACTIVE, named-pool Sandbox creation can still cold-start from its available applied template when no eligible warm member is available. Existing customer Sandboxes continue. A positive target does not guarantee ready capacity. Existing service capacity validation still applies. [required]

params.name: container_image
params.help: Required for CUSTOM and must be omitted for MANAGED. A CUSTOM image must be a digest-pinned same-region OCIR reference, using sha256 with exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The CP workflow prepares the template through the data plane, reusing current BYOC image and Project identity validation. Successful configuration does not guarantee image pull or runtime readiness.

sandbox-warm-pool delete.help:
Deletes a named MANAGED or CUSTOM pool through a CP Work Request. Reserved MANAGED default entries cannot be deleted and return 409. CP persists DELETING and closes admission as the new configuration propagates, drains idle members and deletes the pool resource. The management response does not promise immediate global admission closure or completed cleanup. Already-adopted customer Sandboxes survive and retain required template dependencies. Get and List continue to show DELETING until pool cleanup completes. The CP then records DELETED and releases the name. Name reuse always allocates a new id and materialized names. Retained templates may outlive the pool while customer Sandboxes still depend on them. A repeated delete during DELETING returns the existing Work Request. A missing name returns 404. After name reuse, the path identifies the new pool; use the original if-match ETag to prevent deleting it. Conflicting operations return 409 and stale if-match returns 412. 
[Command Reference](deleteSandboxWarmPool)

sandbox-warm-pool update.help:
Only desiredCapacity may change. If desiredCapacity is omitted, the current desired capacity is preserved. An empty update object is allowed; an explicit null value for desiredCapacity is not allowed. Named MANAGED and CUSTOM pools and reserved MANAGED defaults can be resized. Default-pool updates use the existing Project configuration workflow; no separate desired configuration is created for those entries. CP persists UPDATING and a Work Request, applies the desired replica count, then returns the pool to ACTIVE after verifying the configuration. The workflow does not wait for ready members. Zero pauses idle prewarming. Once the pool is ACTIVE, named-pool Sandbox creation can still cold-start from its available applied template when no eligible warm member is available, regardless of the capacity target. Already-admitted Sandboxes continue. Unnamed Sandbox creation retains its existing behavior. Concurrent management operations return 409. If provided, if-match must match the current configuration ETag; otherwise this operation returns 412. 
[Command Reference](updateSandboxWarmPool)

params.help: Owning Generative AI Project OCID. Resolve parent compartment for authorization. [required]

params.name: name
params.help: Immutable name within the Project. [required]

params.name: desired_capacity

params.name: schedule_config_time_start
params.help:
The schedule starting date time, if null, System set the time when schedule is created. Format is defined by [RFC3339].
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
